title: Forward implication for pointwise basic-open detection
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], L an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], S its graded section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], and f:X -> Proj(S) [def-pc-proj]. Assume for every homogeneous u of positive degree r, every n >= 0, and every homogeneous xi of degree nr, that on f^{-1}(D_+(u)) the restricted tensor-power sections satisfy f^sharp(xi/u^n) u^n = xi. Let x admit a homogeneous section t of some degree e > 0 nonvanishing at x [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Let s be homogeneous of degree d > 0. If f(x) belongs to D_+(s), then s is nonvanishing at x.

proof.text: Use the nonvanishing/local-generation equivalence. An isomorphism transports local free generators in both directions, so it preserves nonvanishing. For two invertible modules choose simultaneous local free generators and write the sections as a times one generator and b times the other. Tensor multiplication gives coefficient a*b. The generating-locus basic-open characterization and D(a*b)=D(a) intersect D(b) therefore prove the tensor nonvanishing formula.

proof.text: Extract single-component representatives of homogeneous section-ring elements. DirectSum.of_mul_of and evaluation at the sum of degrees identify their product component with tensor multiplication transported through tensorPowAddIso. The preceding tensor and isomorphism calculations, followed by induction on the positive exponent, show that the degree-n*d component of s^n has precisely the nonvanishing locus of the degree-d component of s. The degree-one base case is the identity; at a positive successor, intersect the induction locus with the original locus.

proof.text: Choose the positive-degree section t supplied by hx. The homogeneous element t^d has degree d*e=e*d and is nonvanishing at x by positive-power invariance. Apply hformula for s with exponent e and this numerator. On the inverse image of D_+(s), the restricted numerator is a scalar multiple of the restriction of s^e. Taking germs at x respects both restriction and scalar multiplication; the maximal-ideal submodule is closed under scalar multiplication. Consequently nonvanishing of the numerator forces nonvanishing of s^e. Positive-power invariance then gives nonvanishing of s.

theorem sectionRing_proj_mem_basicOpen_forward (X : Scheme.{v}) (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (f : X ⟶ Proj (sectionRingGrade L))
    (hformula : ∀ (d : ℕ) (_hd : 0 < d) (s : sectionRingGrade L d),
        ∀ (n : ℕ) (ξ : sectionRingGrade L (n • d)),
          (f.app (Proj.basicOpen (sectionRingGrade L) s.val)
            (Proj.awayToSection (sectionRingGrade L) s.val
              (HomogeneousLocalization.Away.mk (sectionRingGrade L) s.property n
                ξ.val ξ.property))) •
            (L.tensorPow (n • d)).presheaf.map (homOfLE
              (le_top : f ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen (sectionRingGrade L) s.val ≤ ⊤)).op
              ((s.val ^ n) (n • d)) =
          (L.tensorPow (n • d)).presheaf.map (homOfLE
              (le_top : f ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen (sectionRingGrade L) s.val ≤ ⊤)).op
            (ξ.val (n • d)))
    (x : X)
    (hx : ∃ (e : ℕ) (t : sectionRingGrade L e),
      0 < e ∧ x ∈ nonvanishingLocus (L.tensorPow e) (t.val e))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (s : sectionRingGrade L d) :
    x ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen (sectionRingGrade L) s.val →
      x ∈ nonvanishingLocus (L.tensorPow d) (s.val d)
